Chapter 6 • Covariant Derivative

6.3 Parallel Transport and Autoparallels

  • Let \(\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathcal{M}\) be a smooth curve, with velocity \(v_\gamma : \lambda \mapsto v_{\gamma(\lambda)}\). Since the direction of \(\nabla\) is a single tangent vector, \(\nabla_{v_{\gamma(\lambda)}} \mathcal{Y}\) is defined for every \(\mathcal{Y} \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M}\). The quantities one wants to differentiate along \(\gamma\), however, starting with \(v_\gamma\) itself, are not vector fields on \(\mathcal{M}\), but vector fields along \(\gamma\), i.e. maps \begin{align*} \mathcal{X}_\gamma : \mathbb{R} &\longrightarrow T\mathcal{M} \\ \lambda &\longmapsto \mathcal{X}_\gamma(\lambda) \in T_{\gamma(\lambda)}\mathcal{M}, \end{align*} whose component functions \(x^i_\gamma(\lambda) \coloneqq (dx^i)_{\gamma(\lambda)}\big( \mathcal{X}_\gamma(\lambda) \big)\) are smooth (for those \(\lambda\) with \(\gamma(\lambda) \in \mathcal{U}\)). Examples are the velocity \(v_\gamma\), with component functions \(\dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)\), and the restriction \(\mathcal{Y} \circ \gamma\) of a vector field \(\left. \mathcal{Y} \right|_\mathcal{U} = \tilde{x}^j \, \partial x_j\), with component functions \(\tilde{x}^j \circ \gamma\). The converse fails: if \(\gamma(\lambda_1) = \gamma(\lambda_2)\) but \(\mathcal{X}_\gamma(\lambda_1) \neq \mathcal{X}_\gamma(\lambda_2)\), as for the velocity of a figure-eight curve at its crossing point, \(\mathcal{X}_\gamma\) is not the restriction of any vector field on \(\mathcal{M}\), and \(\nabla\) cannot be applied to it directly.

  • There exists a unique operator \(\nabla_{v_\gamma}\), the covariant derivative along \(\gamma\), mapping smooth vector fields along \(\gamma\) to smooth vector fields along \(\gamma\), such that, for all \(\mathcal{X}_\gamma, \mathcal{Y}_\gamma\) along \(\gamma\), \(\alpha \in \mathbb{R}\) and smooth \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ} : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\):

    1. \(\mathbb{R}\)-linearity: \(\nabla_{v_\gamma} (\mathcal{X}_\gamma + \alpha \, \mathcal{Y}_\gamma) = \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma + \alpha \, \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{Y}_\gamma\).

    2. Leibniz rule: \(\nabla_{v_\gamma} (\textrm{\runic ᚱ} \, \mathcal{X}_\gamma) = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}' \, \mathcal{X}_\gamma + \textrm{\runic ᚱ} \, \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma\).

    3. Compatibility with \(\nabla\): if \(\mathcal{X}_\gamma = \mathcal{Y} \circ \gamma\), then \(\big( \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma \big)(\lambda) = \nabla_{v_{\gamma(\lambda)}} \mathcal{Y}\).

    In a chart \((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X})\) it reads \begin{equation*} \big( \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma \big)(\lambda) = \Big( \frac{d x^k_\gamma}{d\lambda}(\lambda) + \left(\Gamma_\mathscr{X}\right)^k_{ji}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, x^j_\gamma(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \Big) (\partial x_k)_{\gamma(\lambda)}. \tag{$\ast\ast$} \end{equation*} Proof. As for \(\nabla\), \(\nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma\) at \(\lambda\) only depends on \(\mathcal{X}_\gamma\) near \(\lambda\), so it suffices to work on an interval of parameters along which \(\gamma\) stays in \(\mathcal{U}\). Uniqueness: there, \(\mathcal{X}_\gamma = x^j_\gamma \, (\partial x_j \circ \gamma)\), so properties 1 and 2, then 3, and finally property 4 of \(\nabla\) force \[ \big( \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma \big)(\lambda) = \frac{d x^j_\gamma}{d\lambda}(\lambda) \, (\partial x_j)_{\gamma(\lambda)} + x^j_\gamma(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \nabla_{(\partial x_i)_{\gamma(\lambda)}} \partial x_j, \] which is \((\ast\ast)\). Existence: define \(\nabla_{v_\gamma}\) chart by chart through \((\ast\ast)\). Properties 1 and 2 are immediate. For property 3, the expansion of \(\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} \mathcal{Y}\) derived above, at \(\mathcal{X}_p = v_{\gamma(\lambda)}\), coincides with \((\ast\ast)\) for \(x^j_\gamma = \tilde{x}^j \circ \gamma\), since \(v_{\gamma(\lambda)}(\tilde{x}^k) = (\tilde{x}^k \circ \gamma)'(\lambda)\). On chart overlaps, both chart expressions satisfy properties 1–3, so by uniqueness they coincide. \(\square\)

  • We define, for all \(\lambda \in \mathbb{R}\): \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \begin{array}{c} \text{A vector field } \mathcal{X}_\gamma \text{ along } \gamma \text{ is}\\ \text{\textbf{parallelly transported} along } \gamma \text{ if} \end{array} & \begin{array}{c} \text{A smooth curve } \gamma \text{ is}\\ \text{\textbf{autoparallelly transported} if} \end{array} \\[8pt] \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma = 0. & \nabla_{v_\gamma} v_\gamma = 0. \\[12pt] \hline \\[-6pt] \begin{array}{c} \text{A vector field } \mathcal{X}_\gamma \text{ along } \gamma \text{ is}\\ \text{\textbf{parallel} along } \gamma \text{ if} \end{array} & \begin{array}{c} \text{A smooth curve } \gamma \text{ is}\\ \text{\textbf{autoparallel} if} \end{array} \\[8pt] \big( \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma \big)(\lambda) = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\lambda) \, \mathcal{X}_\gamma(\lambda). & \big( \nabla_{v_\gamma} v_\gamma \big)(\lambda) = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\lambda) \, v_{\gamma(\lambda)}. \end{array} \] where \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ} : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\) is a smooth function. We define the acceleration of the curve \(\gamma\) as \(a_\gamma(\lambda) \coloneqq \big( \nabla_{v_\gamma} v_\gamma \big)(\lambda) \in T_{\gamma(\lambda)}\mathcal{M}\). Parallel transport cannot, in general, be phrased in terms of vector fields on \(\mathcal{M}\): transporting a vector around a closed curve typically returns a different vector, so the transported vectors are not the values of any single vector field on \(\mathcal{M}\). This failure to return, the holonomy of \(\nabla\), is closely related to the curvature introduced below.

  • Applying \((\ast\ast)\) to \(\mathcal{X}_\gamma = v_\gamma\), whose component functions are \(x^k_\gamma = \dot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}\), with \(\frac{d}{d\lambda} \dot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) = \big( \mathscr{X}^k \circ \gamma \big)''(\lambda) \eqqcolon \ddot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)\), and using that the \((\partial x_k)_{\gamma(\lambda)}\) form a basis of \(T_{\gamma(\lambda)}\mathcal{M}\), the autoparallel condition \(\big( \nabla_{v_\gamma} v_\gamma \big)(\lambda) = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\lambda) \, v_{\gamma(\lambda)}\) becomes the autoparallel equation \begin{align*} \ddot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) + \left(\Gamma_\mathscr{X}\right)^k_{ji}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \end{align*} which, for autoparallelly transported curves (\(\textrm{\runic ᚱ} \equiv 0\)), reads \begin{equation} \boxed{ \ddot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) + \left(\Gamma_\mathscr{X}\right)^k_{ji}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) = 0, } \tag{6.1} \end{equation} a system of \(d\) second-order ordinary differential equations for the chart representative \((\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma)(\lambda)\). When all the \(\Gamma_\mathscr{X}\)’s vanish, as for the Euclidean plane in the cartesian chart with its standard connection, its solutions are straight lines.
